newSounds: j = throaty H (like Telugu హ but from the throat), ñ = ny in canyon, rr = Telugu ర trill
rhythm: syllable-timed — close to Telugu, so the rhythm is easy for you
registerFirst: usted — the polite form. Locals will invite you to drop it; that is a compliment
trap: b and v sound the same; h is always silent (Hola = OH-lah); z and c before e/i are s in Latin America but th in Spain
